title.narrative: Operating the health care system for earthquake victims in northwestern Syria3

description.narrative: Continuing to activate the work of mobile field teams consisting of 9 mobile clinics equipped with the urgent medical response project for those affected by the earthquake, funded by the King Salman Center for Relief and Humanitarian Action, consisting of mobile medical teams that make periodic visits to provide health and nutritional care services to the displaced in camps, shelters, and areas generally affected by the earthquake, so that services are provided to most of those affected by the effects of the earthquake that struck Syria, in light of the inability of local authorities to provide medical services to them due to the large numbers and the weakness of health capabilities in Syria in the first place. The medical teams will be distributed across 9 main areas that contain more than 3,000,0000 people, a large part of whom have lost most of what they own except the tents in which they live. The project aims to provide primary health care services and seeks to raise the level of public health for the displaced and ensure prevention and appropriate treatment for diseases prevalent in the camps and gatherings in which they live and try to prevent the spread of epidemics and infectious diseases. All cases that need referral will be referred to the hospitals covered by the project / insurance Distribution of baby milk to those affected by the earthquake

Providing integrated and field healthcare services, psychological, social and nutritional support, participating in routine vaccination campaigns, and providing all diagnostic and therapeutic health services, surgeries and medicines to alleviate the suffering of those affected by the earthquake by providing a diverse medical response in a number of Syrian regions. It is expected that 251,307 people will benefit from the project on a regular and free basis.

Readiness of hospitals to provide secondary and tertiary healthcare services to 140,000 beneficiaries of earthquake-affected residents and displaced persons in northwestern Syria, readiness of field teams to provide healthcare, nutrition, psychological and social health, diagnostic and therapeutic services in IDP camps and temporary shelters in earthquake-affected areas in northwestern Syria for 110,000 beneficiaries, provision of secondary and tertiary healthcare services to (140,000) beneficiaries, provision of field healthcare services to (110,000) beneficiaries, provision of an interconnected database between field teams and associated specialized hospitals and development, expansion and strengthening of the medical referral system and early detection of diseases and reducing the spread of epidemics and infectious and contagious diseases in IDP camps and temporary collective shelters, strengthening the economic situation of the project staff, numbering (307) employees in addition to their families, reducing the migration of specialized staff and reuniting and their steadfastness in providing health services to their community, reducing the spread of malnutrition among children and alleviating Human suffering of 1,000 children and their families by providing 36,000 cans of baby milk so that each child gets his full milk needs monthly for a whole year.
